name: Toy Figure
traits: compact collectible proportions: big head, short stubby limbs
moulded plastic with satin or gloss finish, seams and paint edges
miniature dioramas shot like a product photo
bestFor: collectible or series ads with recurring characters
comedy where small figures take on a big problem
suits: small products that can sit at toy scale (bottles, snacks, gadgets, cosmetics); playful, collectible brands
stylePara: Collectible toy-figure look, photographed like a tabletop product shoot: characters are small moulded vinyl figures with compact proportions, a large head about half the body height, short stubby limbs and simplified mitten-like hands; satin plastic with crisp specular highlights, faint mould seams and tiny paint-application edges; eyes are painted, never wet; visible joints at neck, shoulders and hips; sets are miniature dioramas with slightly oversized props; macro-lens shallow depth of field, soft-box key light with a clean rim, everything at toy scale.

rendering.line: no outlines: crisp moulded edges and painted borders between colour areas
rendering.shading: glossy or satin plastic shading with sharp soft-box reflections and slight translucency at thin edges
rendering.colour: clean factory paint colours, each part one solid hue; product colours exact
rendering.texture: smooth plastic with mould seams, tiny paint overspill, a little dust at macro scale
rendering.lighting: large soft box key, white bounce card fill, hair-light rim; small tabletop scale

motion: Pick one mode per ad. Rigid toy stop-motion: figures repositioned on twos, bodies never bend, limbs rotate only at their joints. Or living toy: the same rigid plastic parts moving smoothly at the joints. In both, the plastic never deforms and faces stay as painted; expression changes happen on a cut.
camera: Macro lens 60-100 mm at tabletop height, slow slider moves, focus pulls between figure and product; the shallow focus is what sells the miniature scale.
avoid: plastic bending like rubber at elbows and knees
moulded logos or stamps on the base or back
sheets: Each figure as a boxed-collectible turnaround (front, three-quarter, side, back) on a seamless pale backdrop, with the joint positions and the head-to-body ratio described in the prompt and an unmarked base; the product as a toy-scale miniature beside the figure plus a straight-on packshot with the exact label.
risk: Seedance wants to bring the toys to life: elbows bend, faces gain expressions and the plastic turns into skin. Choose rigid or living-toy timing and write it in MOTION; keep expression changes to cuts. It also invents moulded logos and copyright stamps on bases and backs; say 'unmarked base, no moulded lettering' in NO TEXT.

example.prompt: Collectible toy-figure still, macro product photography: a small satin vinyl figure of a woman in her thirties with a large head, a moulded dark bun, painted eyes and a glossy orange top holds a tiny green glass bottle with a yellow cap in mitten-like hands, standing in a miniature sunny kitchen diorama; a droopy miniature fern sags on the windowsill; soft-box key with a clean rim, crisp plastic highlights, faint mould seams, shallow depth of field, unmarked base. Vertical 9:16. No text.
